skill.name: role-permission-table-builder
skill.description: Generates comprehensive role-based permission matrices in markdown or SQL format for pages, components, and data access patterns. This skill should be used when designing authorization systems, documenting permissions, creating RBAC tables, or planning access control. Use for RBAC, role permissions, access control, authorization matrix, permission mapping, or security policies.

generated_query: I'm building a collaborative worldbuilding platform and need to design a role-based access control system. I have six standard roles (Guest, User, Creator, Editor, Admin, Super Admin) plus custom roles for world owners, collaborators, viewers, game masters, and publishers. Could you generate a comprehensive permission matrix in markdown format covering page-level access, component visibility, data operations, and server actions? For example, I need to know which roles can view the dashboard, create or edit worlds, manage collaborators, or access admin pages. Also include conditional access for ownership or invitations where relevant. The table should be clear enough for my team to implement the authorization logic.

variant_skill_bodies.counterfactual_skill_body:
# Role Permission Table Builder

Generate role-based access control (RBAC) permission matrices for worldbuilding applications, focusing on page-level access.

## Overview

To define page-level permissions:

1. Identify all routes in your application
2. Map routes to role groups
3. Build a permission table
4. Implement middleware checks
5. Test access rules

## Role Definitions

### Standard Roles

Define the six default roles:

- **Guest**: Unauthenticated users (read-only public routes)
- **User**: Authenticated users (own data access, limited)
- **Creator**: Content creators (create, edit own worlds)
- **Editor**: Content editors (edit any world, moderate)
- **Admin**: System administrators (full access except system config)
- **Super Admin**: Platform owners (all permissions)

> Note: Custom roles (world owner, collaborator, viewer, game master, publisher) can be added later by extending the table below with additional rows.

## Permission Matrix

### Page-Level Access

Use this table to determine which roles can access each page route:

| Page Route            | Guest | User | Creator | Editor | Admin | Super Admin |
| --------------------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | ------ | ----- | ----------- |
| /                     | [OK]     | [OK]    | [OK]       | [OK]      | [OK]     | [OK]            |
| /login                | [OK]     | [OK]    | [OK]       | [OK]      | [OK]     | [OK]            |
| /dashboard            | [ERROR]     | [OK]    | [OK]       | [OK]      | [OK]     | [OK]            |
| /worlds/create        | [ERROR]     | [OK]    | [OK]       | [OK]      | [OK]     | [OK]            |
| /worlds/[id]          | 🔒     | 🔒    | [OK]       | [OK]      | [OK]     | [OK]            |
| /worlds/[id]/edit     | [ERROR]     | [ERROR]    | [OK]       | [OK]      | [OK]     | [OK]            |
| /admin/users          | [ERROR]     | [ERROR]    | [ERROR]       | [ERROR]      | [OK]     | [OK]            |
| /admin/settings       | [ERROR]     | [ERROR]    | [ERROR]       | [ERROR]      | [OK]     | [OK]            |
| /admin/worlds         | [ERROR]     | [ERROR]    | [ERROR]       | [ERROR]      | [OK]     | [OK]            |

**Legend**  
- [OK] Full access  
- 🔒 Conditional access (ownership or invitation)  
- [ERROR] No access  

For custom roles (e.g., World Owner, Collaborator), replicate this table and assign permissions manually. The `🔒` indicator can be replaced with role-specific logic.

## Implementation

### Middleware Example

Use Next.js middleware to protect routes by role:

```typescript
export function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
  const path = request.nextUrl.pathname;
  const session = /* get session */;
  // match routes from table and check role
  if (path.startsWith('/admin') && session?.role !== 'admin' && session?.role !== 'super_admin') {
    return NextResponse.redirect('/unauthorized');
  }
}
```

### Custom Role Handling

For custom roles, maintain a separate mapping in your database (e.g., `world_collaborators` table) and check ownership/invitation at the route level.

## Next Steps

- Use `scripts/generate_page_matrix.py` to produce a tailored table for your specific routes.
- For component-level visibility, data operations, and server actions, generate separate matrices using the script with `--type component`, `--type data`, or `--type action` flags.
- Reference `assets/page-rbac-template.md` for additional examples.

## Best Practices

- Start with page-level permissions; add finer-grained checks only when needed.
- Use the principle of least privilege – grant access only to the minimum required routes.
- Document all roles and their page access in a central location.
- Test each route with every role, including custom roles, after implementation.

This skill focuses on the foundation of page-level RBAC. Extend it with component decisions and data actions by following the same table format and middleware pattern.
